Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on recombinantly produced human thyroglobulin (rTG) expressed in HEK293T cells. The material was purified via Ni-NTA affinity and size-exclusion chromatography before being crosslinked and analyzed, fitting the 'purified protein or complex' scope.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry component of this study is a structural validation experiment using chemical cross-linking (XL-MS) to confirm the 3D architecture of thyroglobulin. While the broader paper contains differential mutagenesis and hormone production assays, the MS data itself is not a perturbation or differential proteomics study, but rather a structural mapping effort. Therefore, it is mapped as un-classified.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) was used on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos, though the primary goal was identification of crosslinks rather than relative quantification.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment explicitly uses BS3 (bis(sulfosuccinimidyl)suberate) for chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to validate the protein structure.

workflow: Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics
incubated for 2 h on ice at 0.5 mg/mL with or without 1 mM BS3 (bis(sulfosuccinimidyl)suberate, Thermo Fisher)
crosslink search was performed using Xi
BS3’s reaction specificity was restricted to the side chains of lysine, serine, threonine, tyrosine, as well as the protein N termini
search_parameters: Carbamidomethylation on cysteine was set as fixed; oxidation on methionine, hydrolysed/aminolysed BS3 from hydrolysis or ammonia quenching on a free cross-linker end were set as variable modifications.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: This is a structural proteomics experiment using XL-MS. Standard bottom-up pipelines for protein quantification are not applicable; a specialized cross-linking search engine (like Xi) is required to identify residue-pair constraints.
